claims.claim: A user purchase prediction at time t must compute features only from information available by t, while its future seven-day label comes from later events.
claims.notes: A target definition and observation window are explicit, not sourced benchmark results.

claims.claim: Historical feature joins enforce event-time correctness and must account for data availability, not blindly use the latest value.
claims.notes: available_at may differ from source event time and needs production validation.

claims.claim: TimeSeriesSplit uses chronological ordering and supports a gap parameter to separate training and evaluation observations.
claims.notes: The custom sample uses calendar-time gaps matched to the label horizon, not an off-the-shelf index count.

claims.claim: Seven-day future labels must be mature by the next evaluation period; a seven-day embargo is one sufficient toy rule under complete on-time labeling.
claims.notes: Late labels, correlated entities and ingestion delays may require a longer or more specific boundary.

claims.claim: Thresholds must be chosen on validation/CV data, not the final untouched test partition.
claims.locator: Threshold tuning, selection bias and CV guidance
claims.notes: Toy cost ratio 1:5 is illustrative, not a real coupon utility function.

claims.claim: Training preprocessing belongs inside a Pipeline to avoid validation/test data leakage and maintain a coherent inference artifact.
claims.notes: Same code path cannot by itself prove as-of correctness of external feature sources.

claims.claim: Purchase probability P(Y|X) differs from the causal uplift of sending a coupon; randomized treatment/control groups support estimating an average effect under design assumptions.
claims.notes: The example uses an artificial treatment effect and random assignment; cannot represent real company uplift.

claims.claim: A production ML release requires dependency, data, training code, model, evaluation, schema and monitoring lineage, not only a serialized estimator.
claims.locator: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
claims.notes: Auditability/rollback contract is an engineering requirement, not a claim of deployed service.

claims.claim: Joblib serializes Python objects and cannot safely load untrusted artifacts; hash verifies file integrity but not provenance or safety.
claims.notes: Toy persistence example only reloads its own freshly created artifact.

claims.claim: Model metrics from generated user event features are synthetic diagnostic outputs, not real e-commerce benchmark results.
claims.notes: No external production dataset used; the generated label model is known by construction.
